_source.description: Global indium production sites — zinc smelters and refineries with indium recovery circuits
_source.origin: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024, Indium chapter (https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2024/mcs2024-indium.pdf); Indium Corporation technical publications (https://www.indium.com/); S&P Global Market Intelligence smelter profiles; Korea Zinc, Dowa Holdings, Nyrstar, Umicore, Teck Resources, and Zijin Mining annual reports and SEC/ASX/KRX filings; International Lead and Zinc Study Group (ILZSG) statistics (https://www.ilzsg.org/); Roskill/Fastmarkets Indium Market Report 2023
_source.license: USGS: public domain; company data: fair use summary; ILZSG: subscription data summarized under fair use
_source.notes: Indium is almost exclusively a byproduct of zinc refining — there are no dedicated indium mines. Sites listed are zinc smelters/refineries with known indium recovery circuits. Capacity figures represent indium metal recovery capacity where publicly reported; many Chinese facilities do not disclose indium-specific capacity. Coordinates from company filings, USGS MRDS, and satellite verification. Global primary indium production ~900 tonnes/yr (USGS MCS 2024). Secondary (recycled) indium production adds ~1,500 tonnes/yr but is not included here.

_coverage.global_production_source: USGS MCS 2024 — estimated 900 tonnes primary indium
_coverage.known_gaps: Numerous small Chinese zinc smelters with unreported indium byproduct recovery; some Japanese electronics recyclers with secondary indium output; Russian indium production at Chelyabinsk zinc plant (data limited)

sites.name: Zhuzhou Smelter Group
sites.notes: One of China's largest zinc smelters; major indium producer; Hunan Province; integrated In/Ge recovery from zinc residues

sites.name: Liuzhou China Tin Smelter
sites.notes: Guangxi Province; recovers indium from tin-zinc smelting residues; one of the earliest Chinese indium recovery operations

sites.name: Yunnan Chengfeng Non-ferrous
sites.notes: Qujing, Yunnan Province; dedicated indium extraction from zinc concentrates; near Lancang and Jinding zinc deposits

sites.name: Nandan Tin (Guangxi)
sites.notes: Nandan County, Guangxi; processes tin-zinc ores from local Dachang tin polymetallic deposits; significant indium byproduct

sites.name: Zijin Mining Bayannur Smelter
sites.notes: Inner Mongolia; processes zinc concentrates from multiple Zijin-owned mines; integrated indium recovery circuit added 2018

sites.name: Huludao Zinc Smelter
sites.notes: One of China's oldest zinc smelters; Liaoning Province; significant indium recovery from zinc leach residues

sites.name: Shaoguan Smelter
sites.ownership: Shenzhen Zhongjin Lingnan Nonferrous Metals (listed SHE:000060)
sites.notes: Guangdong Province; large integrated lead-zinc smelter; indium recovered from zinc residues; also significant germanium producer

sites.name: Hanzhong Zinc Industry
sites.notes: Shaanxi Province; zinc smelter processing concentrates from Qinling polymetallic belt; indium recovery circuit

sites.name: Baiyin Non-ferrous Smelter
sites.notes: Baiyin City, Gansu Province; historic copper-zinc smelting complex; indium recovered from zinc processing residues

sites.name: Daxin Smelter (Guangxi)
sites.notes: Daxin County, Guangxi; purpose-built indium extraction facility processing zinc concentrates from the Dachang and nearby polymetallic deposits

sites.name: Korea Zinc Onsan Smelter
sites.notes: World's largest zinc smelter complex; Ulsan; major global indium producer from zinc leach residues; also recovers Ge, Ga, Bi

sites.name: Young Poong Sukpo Smelter
sites.notes: Sukpo, Gyeongsang Province; second-largest Korean zinc smelter; indium recovery from zinc electrolysis residues

sites.name: Dowa Metals & Mining Kosaka Smelter
sites.notes: Kosaka, Akita Prefecture; historic mining district; Dowa's primary indium recovery facility; also processes e-waste for In recovery

sites.name: Akita Zinc Smelter
sites.notes: Iijima, Akita Prefecture; electrolytic zinc refinery with indium byproduct recovery from zinc residues

sites.name: Mitsubishi Materials Naoshima Smelter
sites.notes: Naoshima Island, Kagawa Prefecture; integrated copper smelter and refinery; recovers indium from copper anode slimes and zinc residues

sites.name: Teck Trail Zinc Refinery
sites.notes: Trail, British Columbia; one of world's largest integrated zinc-lead smelting complexes; significant indium and germanium producer from zinc residues

sites.name: CEZinc (Canadian Electrolytic Zinc)
sites.ownership: Glencore (effective control via Noranda Income Fund)
sites.notes: Salaberry-de-Valleyfield, Quebec; electrolytic zinc refinery; indium recovered from zinc electrolysis purification residues

sites.name: Nyrstar Auby Smelter
sites.notes: Auby, Nord-Pas-de-Calais; one of Europe's largest zinc smelters; significant indium and germanium byproduct recovery; electrolytic process

sites.name: Umicore Hoboken
sites.type: precious metals refinery with In recovery
sites.notes: Hoboken, Antwerp; world-leading complex materials recycler; recovers indium from zinc residues, ITO sputtering target scrap, and e-waste; both primary and secondary indium

sites.name: Nyrstar Balen-Wezel Smelter
sites.notes: Balen, Antwerp Province; large European zinc smelter; indium extracted from zinc leach residues during electrolytic refining

sites.name: Nyrstar Budel Smelter
sites.notes: Budel-Dorplein, North Brabant; electrolytic zinc smelter with minor indium byproduct recovery

sites.name: Pertusola Smelter (ex-Portovesme)
sites.notes: Portovesme, Sardinia; integrated zinc-lead smelter; indium recovered as byproduct from zinc leach residues; operations curtailed intermittently due to energy costs

sites.name: Doe Run La Oroya Smelter
sites.notes: La Oroya, Junin; historic polymetallic smelter-refinery complex; indium historically recovered from zinc circuit; intermittent operations due to environmental and financial issues

sites.name: Cajamarquilla Zinc Refinery
sites.notes: Near Lima; large zinc refinery (330,000 tpa Zn capacity); small indium byproduct recovery from electrolytic zinc purification; Peru's main indium source

sites.name: Mopani Copper Mines (Mufulira Smelter)
sites.type: copper smelter with potential In recovery
sites.notes: Mufulira, Copperbelt Province; copper smelter with minor indium recovery from zinc-bearing copper concentrates; limited production data available

sites.name: Chelyabinsk Zinc Plant
sites.notes: Chelyabinsk, Urals; Russia's largest zinc smelter; indium extracted from zinc electrolysis residues; limited production data due to sanctions/restricted reporting

sites.name: Hindustan Zinc Chanderiya Smelter
sites.notes: Chanderiya, Rajasthan; one of world's largest integrated zinc smelter complexes (>1 Mt Zn capacity); pilot indium recovery circuit under evaluation; significant potential given zinc concentrate volume

sites.name: Boliden Odda Smelter
sites.type: zinc smelter — In recovery under evaluation
sites.notes: Odda, Vestland; major European zinc smelter (200,000 tpa Zn); indium recovery circuit under technical evaluation as part of Odda Verk expansion; zinc concentrates from Boliden's Swedish mines contain indium
